To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deletion of γ2 subunits from parvalbumin-positive neurons causes wide-ranging behavioral alterations.
the γ2 subunit of GABAA-type receptors is required for normal behavior in mice, and the loss of the subunit from parvalbumin cells leads to behavioral deficits that are widespread in their effects.

selective removal of γ2-containing GABAA receptors from parvalbumin interneurons in mice leads to behavioral impairments in motor coordination, spatial learning, anxiety, pain sensation, prepulse inhibition and sensorimotor integration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the γ2-subunit of the GABAA receptor on parvalbumic interneurons in the brain.
the behavioral significance of GABAA receptor subtypes in parvalbumin interneurons and the role of GABAA γ2 subunit in the development of behavioral alterations.
the importance of GABAA receptor-mediated synaptic inhibition for the development and function of parvalbumine neurons and their role in the modulation of diverse behavioral functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the γ2 subunit is essential for the proper development and functioning of parvalbumine neurons and the brain as a whole.
the γ2 subunit is not essential for the development of Pv neurons, but is required for their normal function.

the γ2 subunit in Pv cells is important for a number of different behavioral functions, including motor coordination and sensorimotor integration (startle reflex and spatial learning), emotional behavior and nocifensive responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fast inhibition onto Pv cells is important for the development and maintenance of many behavioral functions, and this is particularly evident when this fast inhibition is lost.
GABAA receptors in parvalbumin-positive neurons are essential for the development of normal behavior, and that their loss results in a complex behavioral phenotype.
GABAergic inhibition on parvalbumi neurons is important for a wide range of behaviors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the γ2-containing GABAA receptors are crucial for proper development and function of parvalbumine neurons.
the γ2 subunit of the GABAA receptor is a critical regulator of parvalbumintaining neurons.
fast inhibition onto PV cells is important for a wide range of behaviors.
